scores.claim_text: D-Wave achieved 'awardable' status through the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_federal_presence(name_variants=[D-Wave Quantum, D-Wave Government Inc., D-Wave Systems, D-Wave US Inc., D-Wave Commercial Inc., D-Wave])
scores.interpretation: INFLATION_SUSPECT. D-Wave Government Inc. is registered as a federal contractor (UEI PATGKJM747F7) but has $0 in contracts and $0 in grants across 2018-05/2026. Tradewinds 'awardable' status is a marketplace eligibility flag, not a contract — it confirms that no DoD program has actually obligated dollars to D-Wave. Claim materially overstates federal traction.

scores.claim_text: Davidson Technologies hosts the second U.S.-based D-Wave Advantage2 quantum computer in Huntsville, AL.
scores.interpretation: Davidson Technologies is a real DoD prime with $199M lifetime contracts (Air Force, MDA-adjacent work). The installation of an Advantage2 at Davidson HQ is plausible as a co-location / demo node, but no DoD PE in our J-Book corpus names D-Wave or D-Wave Government as a contractor. Davidson's contracts are NOT funded under a quantum-computing PE — they're cyber, training, and IT-infrastructure awards (e.g., FA861222CB005 'ACC DTC CMCC'). D-Wave's claim that this drives 'United States government customer' revenue is a future-tense aspiration: there is no obligated revenue flowing from a DoD PE through Davidson to D-Wave today. Materiality is moderate because the claim is about deployment, not revenue.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave worked with Davidson + Anduril on a missile-defense planning proof-of-concept (>=10x speedup, +45-60 missiles intercepted).

primary_matches_sample: Ballistic Missile Defense Terminal Defense Segment (PE 0603881C)
Ballistic Missile Defense Midcourse Defense Segment (PE 0603882C)
jbook_missile_defense.note: Multiple MDA PEs are funded but NONE list D-Wave/Anduril/Davidson as primary contractors in the corpus.

scores.interpretation: MDA PEs (BMD Terminal/Midcourse/C2BMC) are real funded programs, but the J-Book corpus shows no D-Wave or Anduril as primary contractor on any of them. The 10-K language 'initial proof-of-concept' is explicit — this is unfunded R&D, not a program of record. There is zero booked revenue from missile defense and no Pentagon PE has obligated dollars to D-Wave. The disclosure is narrative-load-bearing (lead defense story in Item 1) but framework-quantitatively empty. MODERATE because the company is honest about it being a 'PoC'.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave formed a new business unit dedicated to U.S. government adoption, led by a public-sector executive.
scores.interpretation: A federal contracting subsidiary (D-Wave Government Inc.) exists and is SAM-registered, but has obligated $0 across the entire 2018-2026 window — confirmed via UEI-anchored USAspending lookup. A 'new business unit' with a 'seasoned public sector executive' is forward narrative; there is no historical federal revenue base to extend. Combined with C1 and C5 (Customer A is not federal), the U.S. government revenue thesis is structurally unsubstantiated at the cutoff. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY.

scores.claim_text: Customer A = 67% of FY2025 revenue (vs 17% in FY2024); not named.
scores.interpretation: Customer A is ~$16.5M (67% of $24.6M FY2025 revenue) and went from 17%->67% YoY. USAspending shows ZERO federal contracts/grants under any D-Wave name variant, including the UEI-anchored D-Wave Government Inc. — so Customer A is NOT a U.S. federal customer. Cross-referencing the 10-K narrative, the most likely identity is Forschungszentrum Juelich, which 'purchased' the Advantage system in Feb 2025 and upgraded to Advantage2 throughout 2025 (system-sale revenue recognized over the installation period). A single non-US public-research customer driving 67% of revenue is the dominant material risk in QBTS: it inverts the 'broad commercial adoption' narrative the rest of the 10-K paints. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because the concentration is existential AND the customer's identity is suppressed.

scores.claim_text: FZJ purchased the D-Wave Advantage system in Feb 2025 and upgraded to Advantage2 in 2025.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_federal_presence(FZJ) — sanity check that FZJ is non-US

M_value.interpretation_note: FZJ is a German federal research center, expected absence in US data

scores.interpretation: PASS on the FZJ sale claim itself — this is a real, named, externally verifiable customer relationship (FZJ has separately publicized the D-Wave installation). The signal is that FZJ — not the DoD — is the load-bearing revenue customer. This re-frames the entire QBTS revenue story as a single foreign-public-lab system sale, not as Pentagon adoption. Counts as PASS for the literal claim (the sale happened); the *implication* (non-DoD concentration) is captured in C5.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave closed acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc. on Jan 20, 2026.
scores.interpretation: Acquisition coherence score 0.85 — Quantum Circuits' error-corrected superconducting gate-model architecture is technologically continuous with D-Wave's stated pivot from annealing to gate-model. Not a defensive / rollup-distraction acquisition. PASS. Caveat: QCI has only 2 granted US patents, so the technology base being acquired is thin from an IP standpoint, but that does not change the coherence verdict.

scores.claim_text: Gate-model quantum computer will be generally available in 2026.

M_value.note: D-Wave assignee substring picks up huge non-related noise (Aerogel R&D, TransferMyRx, etc.); cannot cleanly verify D-Wave-specific patent rate without disambiguation.

scores.interpretation: Forward technical milestone — by definition not verifiable from disclosure alone. Pre-cutoff signal: only ~5 months between QCI acquisition close (Jan 20 2026) and the stated 2026 GA target is very compressed for productizing an error-corrected gate-model system. Patent base at QCI (2 grants) is small. We mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than red-flagging because this is a roadmap statement, not a revenue claim.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave addresses 'unique research and government classified applications' as a growth market.
scores.interpretation: The three quantum-computing PEs covered in the J-Book corpus are ALL IonQ-anchored (AFRL Quantum Networking, AFRL Qubitekk, UMD Quantum). Two of the three are UNFUNDED_THIS_YEAR / UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS — the broader Pentagon quantum-program budget environment is contracting, not expanding. D-Wave appears in zero of these PEs as a primary contractor. Combined with $0 federal awards via USAspending, the 'classified government applications' growth pillar has no current obligated funding anywhere visible to the framework. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY: the claimed market is funded today only for IonQ-flagged programs (and even those are sunsetting), and D-Wave has no contractor footprint to inherit residual flows. Note: corpus coverage gap — there may be SBIR/STTR-level dollars below the PE-tracking threshold.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave Government Inc. is the primary federal contracting entity.
scores.interpretation: UEI exists, $0 in awards. The subsidiary functions as a registration vehicle without an operating federal contract footprint. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY relative to the framing that the entity is the 'primary federal contracting' arm — primacy implies dollars, and there are none.

scores.claim_text: Quantum systems installed at FZJ (Germany), USC ISI (Marina del Rey), Davidson Technologies (Huntsville, AL), and HQ Burnaby (BC).

M_value.note: All 14 results are unrelated 'TIDAL WAVE' car-wash franchises; no D-Wave facility found under EPA FRS in AL (expected — quantum systems hosted at a third party's site won't be under D-Wave's own EPA registry).

scores.interpretation: EPA FRS absence is consistent with D-Wave being a tenant of Davidson, not the EPA-registered operator. FZJ, USC ISI, and Davidson HQ are all independently externally verifiable counterparties. PASS on the literal facility-existence claim.

PASS on the absolute number. But the arithmetic exposes the underlying story: stripping out Customer A ($16.5M in 2025 vs $1.5M in 2024 implied by 17% share), the non-Customer-A book grew only ~11% YoY ($7.3M -> $8.1M). The 179% top-line growth is essentially one customer (likely FZJ) buying one system. This is consistent with C5 framing the concentration risk.

summary.headline_finding: QBTS is light on the canonical 'named PE / named program' J-Book divergence pattern — the 10-K avoids naming specific Pentagon programs. But the orthogonal verifications hit hard: D-Wave Government Inc. (the federal contracting sub) has $0 in lifetime DoD awards despite Tradewinds 'awardable' status and a 'public sector' business unit; the J-Book quantum portfolio is contracting (2 of 3 quantum PEs UNFUNDED) and D-Wave is named on none; and FY2025 revenue is 67% concentrated in a single undisclosed customer that the 10-K narrative strongly implies is FZJ (a German national lab), not the DoD. The 'DoD growth' pillar is essentially a marketing posture without obligated dollars.
